module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 999

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/999](https://www.erdosproblems.com/999)
- [Er64b] Erdős, P., _Problems and results on diophantine approximations_. Compositio Math.
  (1964), 52-65.
- [KoMa20] Koukoulopoulos, Dimitris and Maynard, James, _On the Duffin-Schaeffer conjecture_.
  Ann. of Math. (2) (2020), 251--307.
-/

@[expose] public section

open MeasureTheory

namespace Erdos999

/-- `x` is *approximable* with respect to `f` if
$$\left\lvert x-\frac{p}{q}\right\rvert < \frac{f(q)}{q}$$
has infinitely many solutions with $(p,q)=1$. -/
def IsApproximable (f : ℕ → ℝ) (x : ℝ) : Prop :=
  {q : ℕ | 0 < q ∧ ∃ p : ℤ, Int.gcd p q = 1 ∧ |x - p / q| < f q / q}.Infinite

/--
For any function $f:\mathbb{N}\to \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ the property that, for almost all
$\alpha$
$$\left\lvert \alpha-\frac{p}{q}\right\rvert < \frac{f(q)}{q}$$
has infinitely many solutions with $(p,q)=1$, is equivalent to
$$\sum_{q\geq 1}\phi(q)\frac{f(q)}{q}=\infty.$$

The Duffin–Schaeffer conjecture. It is easy to prove that the latter follows from the former.
Erdős proved this in the special case when $f(q)q$ is bounded. The full conjecture was proved by
Koukoulopoulos and Maynard [KoMa20].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_999 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ f : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ q, 0 ≤ f q) →
    ((∀ᵐ x : ℝ, IsApproximable f x) ↔
      ¬ Summable fun q : ℕ ↦ (Nat.totient q : ℝ) * f q / q) := by
  sorry

/-- It is easy to prove that divergence of the series follows from approximability almost
everywhere (the Borel–Cantelli lemma). -/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_999.variants.easy_direction (f : ℕ → ℝ) (hf : ∀ q, 0 ≤ f q)
    (h : ∀ᵐ x : ℝ, IsApproximable f x) :
    ¬ Summable fun q : ℕ ↦ (Nat.totient q : ℝ) * f q / q := by
  sorry

/-- Erdős [Er64b] proved the conjecture in the special case when $f(q)q$ is bounded. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_999.variants.erdos (f : ℕ → ℝ) (hf : ∀ q, 0 ≤ f q)
    (hb : ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ q, f q * q ≤ C) :
    (∀ᵐ x : ℝ, IsApproximable f x) ↔
      ¬ Summable fun q : ℕ ↦ (Nat.totient q : ℝ) * f q / q := by
  sorry

end Erdos999

reformulations.difference: The definition requires infinitely many positive denominators admitting a coprime numerator, rather than explicitly requiring infinitely many solution pairs (p,q).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For each fixed positive q, the inequality confines p to the bounded interval (qx − f(q), qx + f(q)), containing only finitely many integers. Consequently, the solution-pair set is infinite exactly when its denominator projection is infinite. This equivalence was proved as Review999.approximable_iff_pairs_infinite in the scratch file.

reformulations.difference: The source's series divergence to infinity is expressed using ¬ Summable for a real-valued sequence indexed by all natural numbers. The same formulation occurs in both variants.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Nonnegativity of f makes every summand nonnegative, so nonsummability is equivalent to partial sums tending to positive infinity. The q=0 summand is zero, and dropping this initial term leaves summability unchanged. Both the divergence equivalence and positive-index reindexing were checked in Lean.

reformulations.difference: The file uses the strict approximation inequality <, matching the problem website, whereas Koukoulopoulos–Maynard's theorem uses ≤.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For fixed f, equality can occur only at the countable collection of endpoints p/q ± f(q)/q. Outside this Lebesgue-null set, every relevant strict inequality is equivalent to its non-strict version. Thus the almost-everywhere approximation assertions are equivalent. This was proved as Review999.strict_weak_ae_iff.

review.notes: All four declarations were checked; no mathematical defect or stale status was found. Erdős's bounded-sequence statement on p. 61 matches the variant after setting ε_q = q f(q), giving error ε_q/q² and series ∑ φ(q)ε_q/q². The website's retrieved LaTeX has an apparent codomain typo, f : ℕ → ℕ; both primary references support the Lean's nonnegative real-valued functions, so this is not a Lean defect. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles successfully and checks the equivalences, zero and single-denominator-support cases, independence from f(0), and satisfiable hypotheses. The recorded equivalence proofs do not depend on sorry axioms. The reviewed file remains identical to its committed blob.
